teams.base: Brackley, Northamptonshire, UK (chassis); Brixworth, UK (Mercedes AMG High Performance Powertrains)

car.name: W17
car.gearbox: Mercedes 8-speed + reverse, hydraulically actuated semi-automatic sequential
car.concept: The W17 keeps push-rod suspension at both ends. Mark Hughes noted push-rods are lighter for the same strength, which helps as teams chase the lower minimum weight. The nose is mounted on pillars to the middle element of the three-element front wing, leaving a large slot underneath to feed the floor. The launch wing looked like a placeholder, and there is no conventional front brake-duct inlet: cooling air is taken between the drum fence and the tyre sidewall. Compact sidepods sit behind high radiator inlets with a strong undercut. In the renders the bodywork kicked up at the rear instead of using the steep downwash of most rivals, although the track car drooped more. Floor boards in the style of old bargeboards are aligned to in-wash front-wheel wake into the floor, and with the venturi tunnels gone the team leans heavily on rear downforce. For Melbourne it declared more downwash bodywork, a higher-camber front wing without a strake, and a higher-camber rear wing whose element chords balance closed-mode downforce against open-mode drag. Dimensions: 5,505mm long, 1,900mm wide, 3,400mm wheelbase; 772kg. [1][2][3][4]
features: Compression-ratio row: rivals suspected Mercedes used thermal expansion to exceed 16:1 when hot. The FIA added a hot test from 1 June 2026, and from 2027 the ratio is measured only at operating temperature.
The FIA's ADUO reviews placed the Mercedes PU 2-4% behind the benchmark (Red Bull), earning one extra homologation in 2026 and one in 2027
A reliability-spec PU update arrived at Austria after early-season retirements
Development was deliberately held back to the second half of the season; the big Malaysia floor package then caused confusion and a split-spec comparison in Singapore
Livery is close to the W16 with silver/black zebra stripes forming the AMG logo; Microsoft replaced INEOS on the airbox

specs.v: Renders and livery revealed 22 Jan 2026. Both drivers ran a roughly 200km shakedown at Silverstone, reported 24 Jan. The car then ran at the private Barcelona test (26-30 Jan), and the team held a launch event on 2 Feb.
Push-rod (carbon wishbones; top wishbone geometry retains anti-dive per Gary Anderson)
Push-rod. The short 3,400mm wheelbase makes a pull-rod hard to package, and rear anti-lift appears retained or increased.

upgrades.items: Bodywork with more downwash in side view and a high inlet; front wing with more camber and no strake; rear wing with more camber and tuned element chords.
upgrades.aim: Pull high-energy flow onto the rear and feed the rear floor, add front load with spanwise loading tuned for the floor, and balance closed-mode downforce against open-mode drag.
upgrades.verdict: Russell took pole and led a Mercedes 1-2.

upgrades.items: Tailpipe repositioned tail-down with a slotted bracket; longer-chord front brake-drum lip.
upgrades.aim: Improve local drag and downforce response, and cut front-corner losses to boost rear downforce.
upgrades.verdict: Minor update. Antonelli won.

upgrades.items: New front wing, front corner, rear corner and floor (reprofiled diffuser roof and sidewall); larger front brake-duct inlets.
upgrades.aim: Better surface flow quality and more local load. The brake-duct inlets were circuit-specific cooling.
upgrades.verdict: Antonelli won. Russell, who started from pole, retired from the lead with a battery-related PU failure.

upgrades.items: Small centreline winglets on the rear wing.
upgrades.aim: Increase downforce.
upgrades.verdict: Not assessed. Hamilton (Ferrari) won; Antonelli retired after a clash with Russell.

upgrades.items: Tweaked front suspension fairings; narrowed engine-cover exit; a Mercedes PU reliability update introduced from this round.
upgrades.aim: Cooling (cover exit). The PU update followed earlier retirements.
upgrades.verdict: Russell won.

upgrades.items: Low-drag Spa rear wing; front wing endplate with more camber on the top edge; revised rear drum winglets.
upgrades.aim: Lower drag (rear wing); no reason stated for the others.
upgrades.verdict: Antonelli won.

upgrades.items: New rear winglet and a tail winglet merging into the rear wing brace; widened rear bodywork exit.
upgrades.aim: Cooling (exit); no reason stated for the winglets.
upgrades.verdict: Not assessed. Norris (McLaren) won.

upgrades.items: Rear wing winglets removed; trimmed rear mirror stays (Monza trim). Spain (R14) followed with a modified rear wing and tailpipe and a reprofiled front drum lip.
upgrades.aim: Reduce drag.
upgrades.verdict: Antonelli won at Monza and in Madrid.

upgrades.items: Major package: new floor (reprofiled diffuser roof, sidewall and winglet, floor boards, leading edge, extra slots, revised floor-corner elements); updated suspension fairings with a new rear corner; rear bodywork tweaks.
upgrades.aim: Performance gains. The package was expected to be worth about 0.3s a lap.
upgrades.verdict: Did not work as expected. Data showed more downforce, but Wolff suggested the car may have lost up to 0.5s. It gained in fast corners and lost in slow ones, possibly on the straights too, on a hot, rough track. Antonelli finished 2nd; Russell's engine failed five laps from the end.

upgrades.items: New front wing and endplate. The team ran a back-to-back comparison of the Malaysia package against the old spec, with Russell reverting to the previous specification. Russell also took a new PU and started from the back.
upgrades.aim: Better performance across the operating envelope, including front-tyre wake control, and an evaluation of the Malaysia upgrade.
upgrades.verdict: Inconclusive. Wolff said the package had not yet delivered the expected gain but was a step in the right direction. Verstappen won.

upgrades.items: No new parts; both cars ran the latest (post-Malaysia) specification.
upgrades.aim: Consolidate understanding of the Malaysia package.
upgrades.verdict: Antonelli won from pole on a one-stop. Russell finished 8th after a 5s penalty.

teams.season: Mercedes has set the benchmark under the new rules. It opened with a 1-2 in Melbourne, won the first six rounds, and has 12 wins from 18 races: nine for Antonelli and three for Russell. The W17 is sharp on turn-in, consistent and strong on traction, and the team has got more from its own power unit than its customers have. Reliability has hurt Russell, with PU failures while leading in Canada and late in Malaysia. Mercedes held development back for the second half, but its big Malaysia floor package confused the team: the data showed more downforce, the stopwatch did not, and it ran split specs in Singapore while Red Bull won twice. With both cars back on the new spec, Antonelli won from pole in Austin to lead Russell by 123 points with five rounds left, and Mercedes leads the constructors' table on 607 points, 133 ahead of Ferrari. [1][2][3][4]
strengths: Best overall package for most of the year: turn-in, mid-corner consistency, traction
Deep power unit knowledge; better exploitation of the M17 than customer teams
Antonelli's form and qualifying (youngest-ever pole and championship leader)
weaknesses: Reliability, especially on Russell's car
Struggles on old, low-grip tarmac and in hot, rough conditions (Malaysia)
Correlation problems with the Malaysia upgrade
Antonelli's race starts at times; Russell's inconsistency
teams.reliability: Mixed. Russell had a battery-related PU failure while leading in Canada (the car's first race retirement) and an engine failure five laps from the end in Malaysia, and took a new PU in Singapore that sent him to the back of the grid. Wolff called the early issues 'not good enough', and a reliability-spec PU followed from Austria.
teams.next: Neither driver had been formally confirmed for 2027 as of 15 Oct 2026. Both are widely expected to stay: The Race understands both hold multi-year deals, and Motor Sport reports Russell's extension clause was triggered in June. Under ADUO, Mercedes has one extra PU homologation for 2027. The fetched sources report no senior staff change. [1][2][3][4]

teams.name: Ferrari

car.name: SF-26
car.fuel: Shell V-Power (sustainable ethanol fuel); Shell Helix Ultra lubricants
car.concept: Ferrari rethought the car's architecture for 2026 and moved to push-rod suspension at both ends. Its opening-race front wing has a narrower span and longer chord, with a single centreline actuator rotating both flaps together for straight mode. The floor is smaller, flatter and simpler, with fewer complex edges, to work across the operating range. The three-element active rear wing was designed not to depend on a beam wing and to maximise the straight-mode effect. In Bahrain testing Ferrari showed a rear wing whose flap flips upside down when opened; rivals later emulated the concept, with Red Bull at Miami and McLaren at Austria. It also introduced a unique exhaust-mounted winglet to steer exhaust gases and extend diffuser flow. After a 'spec A' start, Ferrari ran the most aggressive development programme of the top teams: 11 new parts in Miami and a new front wing, nose, floor and sidepod package in Barcelona. Listed weight is 770kg. [1][2][3][4]
features: Flip-over ('Macarena') straight-mode rear wing concept, later emulated by rivals
Exhaust wing to divert exhaust gases and extend diffuser flow (final Bahrain test)

teams.season: Ferrari has been Mercedes' most consistent challenger. Leclerc was third in Melbourne and Hamilton took his first Ferrari podium in China. The heaviest development programme of the front-runners then brought wins for Hamilton at Barcelona-Catalunya and Leclerc at Silverstone. The chassis is well regarded, but the 067/6 power unit trails the leaders: the FIA judged it more than 4% off the benchmark and granted extra homologations, with updated units in Austria and at Monza. Missed chances at Monaco and Hungary, some late pit calls and no pole positions through Monza have kept it from a title fight. Since the summer it has collected podiums rather than wins: Hamilton came from 18th to third in Malaysia, and Leclerc was second in Singapore and Austin. Ferrari is second on 474 points, with Hamilton third (241) and Leclerc fifth (233). [1][2][3][4]
strengths: Fastest development rate of the top teams; chassis upgrades that work (Barcelona)
Strong race pace and multi-stop strategies
Innovative straight-mode rear wing concept
Hamilton's resurgence; two strong scorers
weaknesses: Power unit deficit to the leaders (ADUO >4% band)
One-lap pace: no Grand Prix poles through Monza

Strategy and execution errors (VSC call in Australia, late pit calls)
teams.reliability: No major pattern reported. Leclerc retired twice in the first 13 rounds. The 'spec A' Fiorano shakedown had a stoppage reported by The Race.
teams.next: Hamilton stays for a third season in 2027. Leclerc signed a multi-year extension in early June that runs well beyond 2027. Ferrari has two extra ADUO PU homologations for 2027. The fetched sources report no senior staff changes. [1][2][3][4]

car.name: RB22
car.fuel: Esso / Mobil Synergy fuel; Mobil 1 lubricants
car.concept: The RB22 has a very narrow nose joined to the front wing by two outboard pylons. The wing's two upper flaps recline in straight mode, and its thick-edged, twisted endplates sit on a large conical footplate. Red Bull moved to a more conventional push-rod front layout with fairings wrapping the arms; Gary Anderson thought anti-dive had been reduced. At launch its sidepods were the most shrink-wrapped on the grid, with the side-impact structure protruding as an 'ear', an inlet with little undercut, and bodywork that falls away abruptly before the floor. Heavily worked floor boards and slotted tyre-spat areas manage tyre wake. Anderson saw a diffuser sidewall cut-out that uses high-energy tyre-squirt flow as a modern blown-diffuser effect. The concept evolved hard in-season: a Ferrari-style rotating straight-mode rear-wing element arrived in Miami and was dropped at Spa, a diffuser inspired by competitor designs came in Hungary, and a Baku floor and sidepod package began its late-season run. Listed weight is 770kg. [1][2][3][4]

The FIA's ADUO analysis rated its combustion engine the strongest on the grid, so it is the benchmark and gets no extra upgrades

Late-season top-speed advantage credited partly to aero efficiency (Automoto.it)

upgrades.aim: Local load and integration of straight and corner modes.
upgrades.verdict: Poor start. Verstappen crashed in Q1 and recovered to 6th; Hadjar qualified 3rd but retired with an engine problem.

upgrades.verdict: Little effect. Gasly's Alpine held Verstappen up for much of the race, and Hadjar finished 12th.

upgrades.aim: More load with stable downstream flow, drawing duct air from higher-pressure sources, and more drag shed in straight mode.
upgrades.verdict: A step: Verstappen scored in both the sprint and the race. Hadjar was disqualified from qualifying for a technical infringement and crashed early in the race.

upgrades.items: New front wing and floor; revised brake ducts and engine-cover cooling exit panels.
upgrades.aim: Performance (wing and floor); cooling for Montreal's braking demands.
upgrades.verdict: Worked. Verstappen finished 3rd for Red Bull's first podium of 2026, and Hadjar was 5th.

upgrades.aim: No reasons stated.
upgrades.verdict: RACER said Red Bull threatened to win in Austria; Russell won.

upgrades.aim: Flow stability, and a response to two incidents for Verstappen in two races.
upgrades.verdict: Rear-wing problems cost Red Bull performance at Spa, after costing points at Silverstone.

upgrades.items: Rear wing with revised pylon profiles and flap geometry; new diffuser described as inspired by competitor designs.
upgrades.aim: No stated aim beyond following rivals' diffuser ideas.
upgrades.verdict: Not assessed. The team scored back-to-back podiums going into the summer break.

upgrades.items: Trimmed front wing endplate; revised floor bib edge; amended rear suspension-to-wheel bodywork and tailpipe bracket. Spain (R14) added rear-wheel bodywork changes and a floor-to-chassis geometry change.
upgrades.aim: More downstream floor load and stability, plus reliability; in Madrid, tackling tyre degradation Verstappen had flagged at Monza.
upgrades.verdict: Not assessed.

upgrades.items: New floor body and diffuser within the permitted geometry; new sidepod to meet the floor; updated cooling louvres; revised mirror and halo fairings.
upgrades.aim: More local load while keeping flow stable.
upgrades.verdict: Worked. It started Red Bull's strong run: Verstappen was 2nd in Baku, then won in Malaysia and Singapore. Automoto.it credits better high and medium-speed direction changes and top speed.

upgrades.items: Minor floor-board geometry revision.
upgrades.verdict: Verstappen took pole and won Red Bull's first race of 2026 in a rain-delayed race; Hadjar was 5th.

upgrades.items: New front wing modified from a previous assembly; enlarged rear brake-duct exits.
upgrades.aim: More local load; cooling.
upgrades.verdict: Verstappen won the sprint and the Grand Prix. Mekies said the recent package was Red Bull's last major upgrade of 2026.

upgrades.items: Optional extra vane on the front-wing footplate carrying a tyre-temperature sensor; revised front-corner gaiter profile.
upgrades.aim: Local load and tyre-surface temperature data; reliability, by reducing tearing risk in the elastomer at full lock.
upgrades.verdict: Mixed. Verstappen took his sixth straight podium (3rd) but called the car undriveable, citing front-wing problems.

teams.season: Red Bull's first season with its own Ford-backed power unit started badly. Verstappen crashed in Q1 in Melbourne, Hadjar's engine failed in that race, Verstappen's gearbox broke in China, and the team briefly dropped to fifth. Rapid aero development from Miami onwards brought a first podium in Canada and a near-win in Austria, although rear-wing problems cost it at Silverstone and Spa, and Hadjar missed three races from Zandvoort, where a wrist injury ruled him out, with Lawson moving up in his place. The FIA's ADUO reviews named its combustion engine the strongest on the grid. From the Baku floor update the RB22 became the pace-setter: Verstappen was second in Baku, then won from pole in the Malaysia-hosted Bahrain GP and again in Singapore. He was third in Austin despite calling the car undriveable. The team is third on 355 points, level with McLaren, with Verstappen fourth (236) and Hadjar eighth (105). [1][2][3][4]
strengths: Strongest combustion engine on the grid per the FIA's ADUO analysis
Late-season top speed and aero efficiency
Improved high and medium-speed direction changes after the upgrades
Verstappen; Hadjar a consistent scorer
weaknesses: Early-season reliability (PU, gearbox)
Rear-wing and straight-mode problems mid-season
Ageing wind tunnel causing correlation issues (Automoto.it)
Car unsettled on upshifts and slow PU response off the start line (Automoto.it)
Tyre degradation (targeted in Madrid)
teams.reliability: Weak early on: Hadjar's engine failure in Australia, Verstappen's gearbox failure in China, rear-wing issues mid-season, and front-corner reliability parts at Zandvoort, Monza and Austin. More solid since late summer, with six straight podiums for Verstappen through Austin.
teams.next: Verstappen extended his contract to 2030 ahead of the Dutch GP. Hadjar is confirmed for 2027 on a new deal announced before his return in Baku. Automoto.it reports Laurent Mekies's contract was extended to 2031. As the ADUO benchmark, Red Bull Ford Powertrains gets no extra PU homologations for 2026 or 2027. [1][2][3][4]

car.name: MCL40
car.gearbox: McLaren 8-speed + reverse; carbon-fibre casing, longitudinal gear cluster, electro-hydraulic seamless shift, epicyclic limited-slip differential
car.concept: The MCL40 launched with a long, rounded, drooped nose that runs well past the front wing. The wing's mounting pylons come out of the sides of the nose, and its flaps are more strongly curved than rivals'. Ramped sidepods with large cooling inlets swept smoothly rearwards, and the early floor boards were closed triangles without the horizontal slots many rivals used. Rob Marshall named packaging the radiators and electrical boxes into the smaller 2026 car as the hardest job. The team chose to learn the rules before chasing lap time, so the Barcelona test car was essentially the Melbourne race car. Active aero uses driver-operated flaps on both wings for Straight Mode and Cornering Mode, and the opening-race rear wing was drawn to maximise cornering load while staying stable when the flap opens. The biggest change came in Baku. A squarer inlet with an outboard dimple formed a double undercut, and an overhanging sidepod replaced the original downwash ramp, exposing more of the floor and feeding cleaner flow to the area between the rear wheel and the diffuser. Team-declared weight is 772kg with driver, with 44-46% on the front axle. [1][2][3][4]
features: Switched to push-rod front suspension, reversing McLaren's previous layout
A two-phase 'new car' package in Miami and Canada was followed by a floor-led Hungary package that won two races in a row
The Baku update changed the sidepod concept from downwash ramp to overhang with a double-undercut inlet; PlanetF1 framed it as a new development direction
At Austria it brought an alternative straight-mode rear-wing activation comparable to Ferrari's flipping 'Macarena' wing
Double non-start in China, traced by Stella to one power unit electrical component; McLaren opened an investigation with Mercedes

teams.season: McLaren's title defence began on the back foot. Piastri crashed on the reconnaissance lap in Melbourne, a power unit electrical fault caused a double non-start in China, and the works Mercedes was clearly quicker. The Miami package brought a sprint win and a 2-3 finish, and a floor-led update in Hungary gave Norris back-to-back wins at the Hungaroring and Zandvoort. Reliability kept costing points: Norris retired in Canada, Monaco (battery) and Baku, Piastri lost Hungary to gearbox damage, and the team has questioned the flow of power unit information from Mercedes HPP. Since the summer the car has looked draggy, with one podium in the five rounds before Austin despite a concept-changing sidepod and floor update in Baku. It is fourth on 355 points, level with Red Bull, with Norris sixth (211) and Piastri seventh (144). [1][2][3][4]

Its signature is the sidepod introduced at the first Bahrain test: an inverted, vertical inlet that runs up the side of the chassis and extends forward, with the side-impact spar hidden inside the bodywork and poking out at the shoulder to form a two-tier shape that manages front-wheel wake. A pelican-style underbelly sculpts the flank, and the downsloping sidepod ramps air onto the floor. For active aero the front wing switched from a single central actuator to twin pods, while the rear wing pivots centrally, likely trading a little drag reduction for a more balanced transition between modes. Gary Anderson read the Bahrain update as an effort to boost front-wing outwash and feed the rear wing and diffuser. Suspension is push-rod at both ends. A 14-part package at Baku renewed the nose, front wing, floor, bodywork and rear wing. [1][2][3][4]

teams.season: Audi's debut started in turmoil: Bortoleto scored with 9th in Melbourne while Hulkenberg did not start, Bortoleto then failed to start in China, and team principal Jonathan Wheatley left after two rounds. Mattia Binotto added the team principal role and Le Mans winner Allan McNish became Racing Director in April. The car's distinctive vertical-inlet sidepods and steady upgrades gave it pace at the lower end of the points, and by late September Audi had scored in five of six Grands Prix. It used one ADUO allowance on a driveability-focused PU update in Barcelona and is saving the second for bigger 2027 hardware. A 14-part Baku package did not score at once, but Hulkenberg was 8th in Singapore. Audi is 8th with 23 points after Austin. [1][2][3][4]

car.concept: Williams went against most of the grid by using a pull-rod front suspension with a push-rod rear, and it takes its gearbox as well as its power unit from Mercedes. James Vowles described the car as roughly three times more complex than any previous Williams. The team skipped Barcelona to protect a thin stock of spares and leaned on its Virtual Track Test rig instead. At launch the team quoted the 772.4kg regulation minimum, but RACER later described the car as late and overweight, and its Baku chassis update brought significant weight savings. The launch renders showed a generic model with little real aero detail. In-season work focused on floor contours and edges, sidepod inlet lips and cooling exits, mirrors, rear impact-structure fairings and the rear brace wing, aiming for more repeatable load over a wider operating window. teams.season: Williams has fallen from fifth in 2025 to ninth. The FW48 was late, missing the Barcelona shakedown, and overweight, a clear step back from 2025. Albon and Sainz scraped 11 points from the first six rounds, which RACER said was more than the car deserved, but Aston Martin's upgrades and stronger Alpine and Racing Bulls form pushed the team back. Its main hope was the Baku package with a lighter chassis and new floor, but Williams brought nothing new to Malaysia, Singapore or Austin and has not scored in the last three races, finishing 17th and 18th at COTA. It has 12 points. [1][2][3][4]

car.concept: Newey describes a holistic package rather than one standout part. The nose and front wing join through the second element rather than the mainplane, so only the upper flap rotates in Straight Mode, and the wide nose with a pelican-style underbelly echoes his 2010-13 Red Bulls. The sidepods are wrapped very tightly around the heat exchangers with a raised midline, leaving a deep gap above the floor reminiscent of old double-floor concepts, while the angled upper surface feeds the coke-bottle region. A triangular airbox with side horns houses the Honda installation. The suspension is placed aggressively for aerodynamic reasons, prompting Williams boss James Vowles to call it very extreme. Like every 2026 car it runs a flatter floor with a stepped diffuser instead of the 2022-25 venturi tunnels. The Hungary B-spec reworked 16 areas, adding a longer, slimmer nose, new front and rear wings and every permitted floor surface, while keeping chassis and front suspension. [1][2][3][4]

teams.season: The AMR26 began as the slowest car on the grid: in testing the Honda RA626H's vibrations damaged its battery system and Stroll put the deficit at around four seconds in Bahrain. Neither car was classified in the first two rounds; Alonso's 18th in Japan was the first finish and his 10th in Monaco the first point. The Hungary B-spec and a new Honda spec at Zandvoort turned things around, with Alonso 9th at Zandvoort and 8th at the Bahrain GP in Malaysia. Reliability is still poor (double retirements at Monza and Baku), and the team is 10th of 11 on 7 points after Austin, all scored by Alonso. In Austin Newey said race pace matched the cars ahead but straight-line speed was lacking. Both drivers are confirmed for 2027. [1][2][3][4]

teams.next: Alonso confirmed a new deal for 2027 on 29 Sep 2026 and Stroll also stays, so the line-up is unchanged. Honda works partnership continues; the team says its short-term focus is closing the performance gap. [1][2][3][4]

car.concept: Cadillac's first car uses a customer Ferrari power unit and gearbox while GM builds its own PU for 2029. Alongside Alpine it was one of two teams to launch with pull-rod front suspension. PlanetF1 called its sidepod relatively benign: a shallow, wide inlet whose corner radius shapes the undercut, with a gently curved upper surface sloping down into the floor. Cooling has been a recurring weak point, addressed with louvre options, reworked brake-duct inlets after Austria and Baku, and a more heavily louvred sidepod in Austin. The team has developed aggressively, with major packages in Miami, Montreal, Monaco (all-new rear wing) and Austria (new sidepod inlets, engine cover, coke profile and floor). It introduced a new front-wing Straight Mode actuator around Monaco/Barcelona. [1][2][3][4]

teams.season: The 11th team is still looking for its first point after 18 rounds; Bottas's 13th in China remains its best result. With a customer Ferrari PU and gearbox, Cadillac has developed more aggressively than anyone else in this group, with big packages in Miami, Montreal, Monaco and Austria, and ran with the midfield in Monaco. But retirements have been frequent, including brake failures and brake-cooling trouble. Graeme Lowdon was replaced as team principal by ex-Alpine and FIA executive Marcin Budkowski on 12 August, described as a planned move from build phase to performance focus. In Austin Bottas stopped with a suspected PU failure, while Perez, about to start his 300th Grand Prix in Mexico, said the car felt closer than expected. Cadillac is 11th with 0 points. [1][2][3][4]
